In the test, the relevant call is `fake.date_time_between(start_date="-2h", end_date={"tz": "invalid", "nested": [1, 2, 3]})`. The provider code I read shows `_parse_date_time` accepts only `(datetime, date)`, `timedelta`, `str`, or `int`. Any other type reaches the final `raise ParseError(f"Invalid format for date {value!r}")`.

For this specific `end_date`, the value is a plain `dict`, so it is not any of the accepted types. Its `repr` in Python is `{'tz': 'invalid', 'nested': [1, 2, 3]}`, matching the literal constructed in the test. Therefore `_parse_date_time` raises `ParseError` with message `Invalid format for date {'tz': 'invalid', 'nested': [1, 2, 3]}`.
